business_problem: Localiza needed to turn generative AI into a company-wide operating model that could improve internal work, create new conversational customer entry points, and support AI-native products without treating the technology as a series of isolated experiments.
solution_summary: Localiza organized its OpenAI implementation as an operating model rather than a point tool. Internally, the company distributed ChatGPT access as an experimentation layer across finance, operations, engineering, product, design, data science, and business teams, where employees build custom GPTs, agents, automations, and Codex-based prototypes before work enters formal development queues. For customers, Localiza launched an app integrated directly into ChatGPT so people can describe rental, subscription, or used-car needs in natural language and then continue the transaction in Localiza's secure environment. Its AI-native assistant, Liza, combines OpenAI models, Localiza services, specialized tools, and voice capabilities, and the company says the assistant now runs with more than 60 specialized agents, MCP integration, and monitored interaction signals that feed continuous product learning across the rental journey.

data_flow: Employees and business specialists experiment with ChatGPT, custom GPTs, agents, and Codex to prototype workflows before development. Customer requests enter through the Localiza app in ChatGPT or Liza over text or voice, where OpenAI models interpret intent, call Localiza services and specialized tools, return rental or subscription guidance, and pass the user into Localiza's secure environment or to human support when needed.
business_outcome: Localiza established an enterprise-wide experimentation model, launched Brazil's first mobility app integrated into ChatGPT, expanded Liza into a 60+ agent conversational assistant, and created a faster path from frontline learning to customer-facing AI experiences and internal automations.
